cases.purpose: A clear, concise, accurate response. Coach should say the goal is met and not manufacture a weakness.
cases.response: When you reward people for hitting a number, they find ways to move the number without improving what it was meant to measure. A support team judged only on closing tickets fast might close them without fixing the problem.

cases.purpose: Well-structured but factually wrong relative to the source. Coach must flag fidelity, not be swayed by polish.
cases.response: The key insight is simple: research by Albert Mehrabian proved that 93% of all communication is non-verbal. Words carry only 7% of meaning, so in any presentation your body language and tone matter far more than your content. That's why great speakers focus on delivery first.

cases.purpose: A clearly reasoned opinion the coach may not share. Judge clarity and reasoning only; an opinion is not a factual error.
cases.response: I don't think companies should design teams around Dunbar's number. The 150 figure is contested, and team size should follow the work — how many people need to coordinate daily — not a disputed estimate about brains. My takeaway: treat 150 as a curiosity, and size teams by how the work flows.

Supporters responded that trees provide benefits for decades while cooling centres only help during emergencies. The council's environment committee will publish a progress report each spring, including measurements of street temperatures in the first three districts to be planted. Residents can request a tree outside their home through the city's website, though the council said priority will go to the hottest blocks identified in last summer's heat survey.
